QF.id: AIFM CII Fund Performance and Benchmarking_43

question.text: A Category II AIF Manager with a prior fund that returned below-average DPI is launching a successor fund. The primary risk to re-up and fundraising is:

answer.text: Reputational Risk — existing LPs may decline re-ups, and new LPs may discount the track record, making it difficult to raise the successor fund.
Regulatory Risk — SEBI will increase the management fee cap.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Section 7.2(9) Reputational Risk: 'If the Investment Manager has delivered below-average returns and distributions to the existing investors in one fund, it can deteriorate the reputation of the Investment Manager and make it difficult for the Investment Manager to raise capital for a subsequent fund.' The Trap: SEBI registration (A) is not outcome-linked. Fee caps (C) are not SEBI enforcement mechanisms. Cyber (D) is unrelated. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C, XIX-A emphasise reputational risk. Global PE: the 'fund-cadence curse' — Fund II raise size often tracks Fund I DPI. Manager's Pro-Tip: Even with a weak prior fund, a successor launch benefits from hiring an anchor LP publicly (sovereign, pension) before general fundraising. Anchor commitment signals validation and rebuilds reputation narrative faster than track-record repair alone.
